title: Ethiopian Chicken Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the everyday chicken stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Everyday Chicken Stew — a simplified, quicker version of Doro Wat for weekday cooking. Chicken pieces simmered in a berbere and kibbeh sauce built on caramelised onions, ready in 60 minutes rather than 2.5 hours. All the essential flavours, practical timing.
longDesc: The everyday chicken stew is what Ethiopian families make when Doro Wat's full ceremony is not practical — a simplified sauce with the same fundamental flavours (berbere, kibbeh, onion, garlic, ginger) but shorter cooking and smaller quantity of berbere. Satisfying and completely Ethiopian.
steps: Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Add chicken pieces. Coat in sauce.
Add water. Simmer covered 45—55 minutes until chicken is falling-tender.
chefTips: Even the simplified version needs 15 minutes of dry-caramelised onion.
Bone-in chicken produces a richer sauce than boneless.
commonMistakes: Skipping or shortening the onion caramelisation.
cookingScience: See ETH061 for Doro Wat science. The shorter cooking time (60 vs 150 minutes) means less collagen conversion from chicken bones — producing a less thick sauce. Adding a small amount of tomato paste compensates by adding body.
culturalNote: The everyday chicken stew is Doro Wat's practical sibling — less ceremonial but no less delicious. Ethiopian families cook it for weekday lunches and quick weekend meals without sacrificing the essential flavour tradition.
